items.meaning: The proper name of the One God, alone worthy of worship
items.explanation: The Name that belongs to Him alone; the other Names are said of Him. Al-Hashr 59:22: He is Allah, there is no god but Him, Knower of the unseen and the seen.

items.meaning: The Most Merciful
items.explanation: From rahmah, mercy. It follows the name Allah in "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Ever Merciful" (al-Fatihah 1:1) and again in 1:3.

items.meaning: The Ever Merciful
items.explanation: Also from rahmah, mercy. It is paired with al-Rahman in al-Fatihah 1:1 and 1:3, and in al-Hashr 59:22.

items.meaning: The King, who owns and rules all things
items.explanation: From mulk, sovereignty. Al-Hashr 59:23 opens its list with it, and Ta Ha 20:114 says: exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth.

items.meaning: The Most Pure, free of every fault
items.explanation: From quds, purity. It comes straight after al-Malik in al-Hashr 59:23 and in al-Jumu'ah 62:1, where all in the heavens and the earth glorify Him.

items.meaning: The Source of Peace, free of every flaw
items.explanation: From salam, peace and soundness. It is named in al-Hashr 59:23, after al-Quddus.

items.meaning: The Giver of Security; the One who affirms the truth
items.explanation: From amn, safety, and iman, affirming as true. It is named in al-Hashr 59:23, after al-Salam.

items.meaning: The Watchful Guardian over all things
items.explanation: From haymanah, watching over and guarding. It is named in al-Hashr 59:23, after al-Mu'min.

items.meaning: The Almighty, never overcome
items.explanation: From 'izzah, might that cannot be overcome. It is one of the most frequent Names in the Quran, often paired with al-Hakim, as at the close of al-Hashr 59:24.

items.meaning: The Compeller, whose will prevails; the One who mends
items.explanation: From jabr, which carries both compelling and setting right what is broken. It is named in al-Hashr 59:23.

items.meaning: The Supreme in Greatness
items.explanation: From kibriya', greatness. It is named in al-Hashr 59:23, which ends: glorified is Allah above what they associate with Him.

items.meaning: The Creator, who brings things into being
items.explanation: From khalq, creating. Al-Hashr 59:24 opens with it: He is Allah, the Creator, the Maker, the Shaper.

items.meaning: The Maker, who brings creation into existence
items.explanation: Named in al-Hashr 59:24, between al-Khaliq and al-Musawwir.

items.meaning: The Shaper, who gives each thing its form
items.explanation: From surah, form. Named in al-Hashr 59:24, which goes on: to Him belong the most beautiful Names.

items.meaning: The Ever Forgiving, again and again
items.explanation: From maghfirah, forgiveness and covering. Sad 38:66 and al-Zumar 39:5 pair it with al-'Aziz.

items.meaning: The Subduer, over whom nothing prevails
items.explanation: From qahr, overpowering. The Quran pairs it with al-Wahid, the One, as in al-Ra'd 13:16 and Ibrahim 14:48.

items.meaning: The Bestower, who gives freely and without return
items.explanation: From hibah, a gift. Al Imran 3:8 asks: grant us mercy from You, You are al-Wahhab. Sulayman asks by it in Sad 38:35.

items.meaning: The Provider of all sustenance
items.explanation: From rizq, provision. Al-Dhariyat 51:58: Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.

items.meaning: The Opener; the Judge who decides between people
items.explanation: From fath, opening, which also means deciding a matter. Saba' 34:26: our Lord will gather us, then judge between us in truth; He is al-Fattah, al-'Alim.

items.meaning: The All-Knowing
items.explanation: From 'ilm, knowledge. The angels say in al-Baqarah 2:32: You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

items.meaning: The Withholder, who restricts as He wills
items.explanation: From qabd, holding in. The Quran uses the verb: Allah withholds and extends (al-Baqarah 2:245). In the list it is paired with al-Basit.

items.meaning: The Extender, who gives generously as He wills
items.explanation: From bast, spreading out. The Quran uses the verb: Allah extends provision to whom He wills, and restricts it (al-Ra'd 13:26).

items.meaning: The Abaser, who lowers whom He wills
items.explanation: From khafd, lowering, and paired in the list with al-Rafi'. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The Exalter, who raises whom He wills
items.explanation: From raf', raising. In Al Imran 3:55 Allah says to 'Isa: I will take you and raise you to Myself.

items.meaning: The Giver of Honour
items.explanation: From 'izz, honour. Al Imran 3:26: You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will.

items.meaning: The Humbler, who abases whom He wills
items.explanation: From dhull, lowliness. Al Imran 3:26: You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will; in Your hand is all good.

items.meaning: The All-Hearing
items.explanation: From sam', hearing. Al-Shura 42:11: there is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

items.meaning: The All-Seeing
items.explanation: From basar, sight. Al-Shura 42:11 pairs it with al-Sami', and al-Isra' 17:1 ends the same way.

items.meaning: The Judge, whose judgement is final
items.explanation: From hukm, judgement. Al-An'am 6:114: shall I seek a judge other than Allah, when He sent down to you the Book explained in detail?

items.meaning: The Just, whose every act is fair
items.explanation: From 'adl, justice and balance. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The Subtle, the Kind, aware of the finest things
items.explanation: Lutf means both gentle kindness and fine subtlety. Al-Mulk 67:14: does He not know, who created? He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

items.meaning: The All-Aware, who knows the inner reality of things
items.explanation: From khibrah, knowledge of the inside of a matter. Paired with al-Latif in al-Mulk 67:14, and with al-Hakim in al-An'am 6:18.

items.meaning: The Forbearing, who does not hasten to punish
items.explanation: From hilm, forbearance. Al-Baqarah 2:225: Allah does not hold you to account for thoughtless oaths, and Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.

items.meaning: The Magnificent, the Supremely Great
items.explanation: From 'azamah, greatness. It ends Ayat al-Kursi, al-Baqarah 2:255: He is the Most High, the Magnificent.

items.meaning: The All-Forgiving
items.explanation: From maghfirah, forgiveness. Al-Zumar 39:53: do not despair of Allah's mercy; Allah forgives all sins; He is the All-Forgiving, the Ever Merciful.

items.meaning: The Appreciative, who rewards and gives more
items.explanation: From shukr, thanks. Fatir 35:30 says He pays people their rewards in full and gives them more; He is Forgiving, Appreciative.

items.meaning: The Most High, above all things
items.explanation: From 'uluww, height. Ayat al-Kursi, al-Baqarah 2:255, ends: He is the Most High, the Magnificent.

items.meaning: The Most Great
items.explanation: From kibar, greatness. Al-Ra'd 13:9: Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Most Exalted.

items.meaning: The Preserver, who keeps and protects all things
items.explanation: From hifz, keeping safe. Hud 11:57: my Lord is Preserver over all things. Saba' 34:21 says the same.

items.meaning: The Sustainer, who gives every creature its nourishment
items.explanation: From qut, nourishment. Al-Nisa' 4:85 ends: and Allah is ever Muqit over all things. The word appears only here in the Quran.

items.meaning: The Reckoner, who suffices
items.explanation: From hisab, reckoning, and hasb, enough. Al-Nisa' 4:6 and al-Ahzab 33:39: Allah is sufficient as Reckoner.

items.meaning: The Majestic
items.explanation: From jalal, majesty. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The Most Generous, the Noble
items.explanation: From karam, generosity and nobility. Al-Infitar 82:6: O man, what has deceived you about your Lord, the Most Generous?

items.meaning: The Watchful, who misses nothing
items.explanation: From muraqabah, keeping watch. 'Isa says in al-Ma'idah 5:117: You were the Watcher over them. Al-Nisa' 4:1 ends: Allah is ever Watchful over you.

items.meaning: The Responsive, who answers those who call
items.explanation: From ijabah, answering. Salih says in Hud 11:61: ask His forgiveness and turn to Him; my Lord is Near, Responsive.

items.meaning: The All-Encompassing, vast in giving and knowledge
items.explanation: From sa'ah, vastness. Al-Baqarah 2:115: wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah; Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.

items.meaning: The All-Wise
items.explanation: From hikmah, wisdom, and hukm, judgement. It closes al-Hashr 59:24: He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.

items.meaning: The Loving
items.explanation: From wudd, love. Al-Buruj 85:14: He is the All-Forgiving, the Loving. Hud 11:90: my Lord is Ever Merciful, Loving.

items.meaning: The Glorious
items.explanation: From majd, glory. The angels say to Ibrahim's household in Hud 11:73: He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.

items.meaning: The Resurrector, who raises the dead
items.explanation: From ba'th, raising up and sending. Surah 22:7: the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and Allah will raise those in the graves.

items.meaning: The Witness, present to everything
items.explanation: From shuhud, being present and bearing witness. Surah 22:17: Allah is Witness over all things. Al-Nisa' 4:79: Allah is sufficient as Witness.

items.meaning: The Truth, whose being is certain
items.explanation: From haqq, what is true and firm. Surah 22:6: that is because Allah is the Truth, He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.

items.meaning: The Trustee, on whom one relies
items.explanation: From tawkil, entrusting. The believers say in Al Imran 3:173: Allah is enough for us, and the best Trustee. Al-An'am 6:102: He is Trustee over all things.

items.meaning: The Strong, whose strength never fails
items.explanation: From quwwah, strength. Surah 22:40: Allah is Strong, Almighty. Al-Shura 42:19 pairs the same two Names.

items.meaning: The Firm, whose strength is unshakeable
items.explanation: From matanah, firmness. Al-Dhariyat 51:58: Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.

items.meaning: The Protecting Friend and Ally
items.explanation: From wilayah, nearness and support. Al-Shura 42:9: Allah is the Protector. Al-Shura 42:28 pairs it with al-Hamid.

items.meaning: The Praiseworthy
items.explanation: From hamd, praise. Fatir 35:15: you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

items.meaning: The Counter, who has numbered all things
items.explanation: From ihsa', counting fully. Al-Jinn 72:28: He encompasses what is with them and has counted all things in number.

items.meaning: The Originator, who begins creation
items.explanation: From bad', beginning. Al-Buruj 85:13: it is He who begins and brings back.

items.meaning: The Restorer, who brings creation back
items.explanation: From i'adah, bringing back. Al-Buruj 85:13: it is He who begins and brings back. Paired with al-Mubdi'.

items.meaning: The Giver of Life
items.explanation: From hayah, life. Al-Rum 30:50: look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He revives the earth after its death; He is the One who gives life to the dead.

items.meaning: The Bringer of Death
items.explanation: From mawt, death. Al-Hadid 57:2: His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death.

items.meaning: The Ever Living
items.explanation: From hayah, life. Ayat al-Kursi, al-Baqarah 2:255, opens: Allah, there is no god but Him, the Ever Living, the Sustainer of all.

items.meaning: The Self-Subsisting, Sustainer of all
items.explanation: From qiyam, standing and upholding. It follows al-Hayy in al-Baqarah 2:255 and Al Imran 3:2, and in Ta Ha 20:111.

items.meaning: The Finder, who lacks nothing
items.explanation: From wujd, finding and having. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The Noble, the Illustrious
items.explanation: From majd, glory, like al-Majid. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The One
items.explanation: From wahdah, oneness. Al-Ra'd 13:16 and al-Zumar 39:4 pair it with al-Qahhar: the One, the Subduer.

items.meaning: The Eternal Refuge, to whom all turn in need
items.explanation: Al-Ikhlas 112:2: Allah, al-Samad. The word is used for one to whom people turn in their needs; it appears only in this ayah.

items.meaning: The Able, who has power to do what He wills
items.explanation: From qudrah, power. Al-An'am 6:65: say, He is the One able to send punishment on you from above you or from beneath your feet.

items.meaning: The All-Powerful, in full command
items.explanation: From iqtidar, full power. Al-Kahf 18:45: Allah has full power over all things. Al-Qamar 54:55 speaks of a Sovereign, All-Powerful.

items.meaning: The One who brings forward whom He wills
items.explanation: From taqdim, putting forward. The Prophet ﷺ said in a supplication in the prayer: You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir (Muslim, 771).

evidence.hadith: Sahih Muslim 771 (Abd al-Baqi numbering), from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: the Prophet's supplication in the prayer, "You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir"

explanationSource.location: Hadith 771 (Abd al-Baqi numbering), narrated by 'Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.meaning: The One who holds back whom He wills
items.explanation: From ta'khir, putting back. Paired with al-Muqaddim in the same supplication of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated by 'Ali (Muslim, 771).

evidence.hadith: Sahih Muslim 771 (Abd al-Baqi numbering), from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: the Prophet's supplication in the prayer, "You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir"

explanationSource.location: Hadith 771 (Abd al-Baqi numbering), narrated by 'Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.meaning: The First
items.explanation: Al-Hadid 57:3: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He knows all things.

items.meaning: The Last
items.explanation: Al-Hadid 57:3: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He knows all things.

items.meaning: The Manifest
items.explanation: From zuhur, being apparent and above. Al-Hadid 57:3 names it with al-Awwal, al-Akhir and al-Batin.

items.meaning: The Hidden
items.explanation: From butun, being within and unseen. Al-Hadid 57:3 names it with al-Awwal, al-Akhir and al-Zahir.

items.meaning: The Governor, who manages all affairs
items.explanation: From wilayah, taking charge. Al-Ra'd 13:11: when Allah wills harm for a people, none can turn it back, and they have no protector besides Him.

items.meaning: The Most Exalted, above all
items.explanation: From 'uluww, height. Al-Ra'd 13:9: Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Most Exalted.

items.meaning: The Most Kind, the Source of all good
items.explanation: From birr, goodness and kindness. The people of Paradise say in al-Tur 52:28: we used to call on Him; He is the Most Kind, the Ever Merciful.

items.meaning: The Accepter of Repentance, who turns to people again and again
items.explanation: From tawbah, turning back. Al-Baqarah 2:37: Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance; He is the Accepter of Repentance, the Ever Merciful.

items.meaning: The Avenger, who requites wrongdoers
items.explanation: From intiqam, requital. Al-Sajdah 32:22: who does more wrong than one reminded of his Lord's signs who then turns away? We will requite the wrongdoers.

items.meaning: The Pardoner, who erases sins
items.explanation: From 'afw, erasing. Al-Nisa' 4:43 and 4:99: Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving. Surah 22:60 says the same.

items.meaning: The Most Compassionate, tender in mercy
items.explanation: From ra'fah, tender compassion. Al-Baqarah 2:143: Allah is Most Compassionate and Ever Merciful to people.

items.meaning: Owner of all Sovereignty
items.explanation: Al Imran 3:26: say, O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and take it from whom You will.

items.meaning: Possessor of Majesty and Honour
items.explanation: Al-Rahman 55:27: all on the earth will pass away, and the Face of your Lord remains, Possessor of Majesty and Honour.

items.meaning: The Equitable, who does justice
items.explanation: From qist, justice. Al Imran 3:18: Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him, upholding justice.

items.meaning: The Gatherer, who brings all together
items.explanation: From jam', gathering. Al Imran 3:9: our Lord, You will gather the people on a Day about which there is no doubt.

items.meaning: The Self-Sufficient, free of all need
items.explanation: From ghina, having no need. Fatir 35:15: you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

items.meaning: The Enricher, who frees from need
items.explanation: From ighna', making free of need. Al-Tawbah 9:28: if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills.

items.meaning: The Preventer, who withholds what He wills
items.explanation: From man', withholding. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The One who brings harm, as He wills
items.explanation: From darr, harm. Al-Fath 48:11: who can do anything for you against Allah if He intends harm for you or intends benefit?

items.meaning: The One who brings benefit
items.explanation: From naf', benefit. Al-Fath 48:11: who can do anything for you against Allah if He intends harm for you or intends benefit? Paired with al-Darr.

items.meaning: The Light
items.explanation: Al-Nur 24:35: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.

items.meaning: The Guide
items.explanation: From hidayah, guidance. Al-Furqan 25:31: your Lord is sufficient as Guide and Helper.

items.meaning: The Originator, who creates without precedent
items.explanation: From ibda', making without any model. Al-Baqarah 2:117: Originator of the heavens and the earth; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, Be, and it is.

items.meaning: The Everlasting, who remains
items.explanation: From baqa', remaining. Al-Rahman 55:26-27: all on the earth will pass away, and the Face of your Lord remains.

items.meaning: The Inheritor, to whom all returns
items.explanation: From irth, inheriting. Al-Hijr 15:23: it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.

items.meaning: The Guide to the right course
items.explanation: From rushd, sound direction. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list

items.meaning: The Patient, who does not hasten
items.explanation: From sabr, patience. It is found in the enumerated list, not as a Name in the Quran.

explanationSource.location: Book of Supplications, hadith 3507 (Ahmad Shakir numbering): the enumerated list
